messages:
Cheng: Heads up — noticed a regression on canary for the cache-hit packing change. p99 latency up ~18% when prefix-hit ratio > 60% :thinking_face:
Amira: ugh. which kernel is flipping? any hot traces? :eyes:
Cheng: profiler snapshot attached below (quick paste):
```
perf:  token-apply-kernel (fastpath)  48.2%
perf:  attention-kernel-v2              31.1%
perf:  matmul-quant (fallback)         14.6%
perf:  overhead/queueing                6.1%
```
Cheng: When prefix hits dominate, batch virtual-length drops and runtime picks matmul-quant fallback more often. matmul-quant has higher p99 on our GPU for short sequences.
Ben: hmm that implies our admission logic is shrinking batches when cache hits are present — reduces kernel utilization -> kernel selector chooses different kernel. Did you capture batch size distribution?
Cheng: Yep. Before: mean batch tokens ~ 2048, after: mean ~ 980, tail gets ~300 tokens.
Amira: Any change to token budget targets or prefill windowing recently?
Cheng: We tightened prefix-prefill margin to reduce latency for cold queries (PR #3120). That lowered allowed slack so cache-hit requests are admitted earlier but grouped into smaller microbatches.
Sara: So smaller microbatches => different kernel and worse throughput per-GPU. We should either increase margin for hit-heavy paths or adjust kernel selection thresholds to prefer fastpath for small batches.
Ben: I lean towards a queue-policy variant: if prefix-hit ratio > X, we relax min-virtual-length target by Y% to preserve kernel choice. That keeps batch composition stable.
Amira: Agree but need safety net for latency SLOs. Maybe do dynamic margin: margin = base_margin * (1 + alpha * hit_ratio). alpha tuned to keep p99 under threshold.
Cheng: Quick A/B numbers from a local sim:
- baseline (no hit-aware relax): p99=122ms, throughput=860 req/s
- relax margin 30% on hit path: p99=135ms, throughput=1050 req/s
- relax margin 15%: p99=126ms, throughput=980 req/s
So a small relax improves throughput but increases tail slightly.
perf-bot: ALERT: perf-regression-detected canary — p99 increased 18% vs prod baseline. Ticket created: INF-4981
Sara: For rollout strategy, do canary with 5% traffic, enable hit-aware-relax=15%, monitor p99, cpu/gpu util, and kernel flip rate.
Ben: Also add metric: kernel_selector_choice_count{kernel=\"matmul-quant\"} and virtual_batch_tokens histogram. We'll need an eval harness to replay prefix-heavy traces.
Amira: Repro steps I ran locally:
1) checkout: git checkout fix/prefetch-margin-experiment
2) start local runtime: ./tools/run_local.sh --batcher-config batcher/exp-relax.yaml
3) replay trace: tools/replay_trace.py traces/prefix-heavy.json --rate 200
Log snippet: `kernel_flip_rate=0.32 -> 0.08` when relax=0.15
Cheng: Action items: @Ben add metric panels + alert tweak; @Sara create canary job with 5% traffic; @Amira run grid (alpha in {0.05,0.15,0.30}) and dump kernel flip vs p99; I'll prepare PR to wire hit_ratio signal into admission controller.
Sara: I'll schedule canary for tomorrow 10:30 UTC and tag oncall.
Ben: For longer term: consider training kernel selector to be cache-aware (cost model should include effective utilization loss from smaller microbatches). Might be better than heuristics.
Amira: agree. short term heuristics + canary, long term cost model.
Cheng: one more note — we saw quant fallback is particularly bad on seq_len<=64. Suggest special-case: if seq_len<96 and kernel_flip predicted, prefer float-kernel even if compute heavier, because p99 better. We'll log that as RFC.
perf-bot: NOTE: experiment started (ID: exp-1392) — monitoring dashboards: /dashboards/prefetch-margin-exp
Sara: cool. wrap up: small rollout, monitor kernel flip rate and p99, iterate alpha. Ping here with results. :thumbsup:
